source: Kim, Sclar, Zhi-Xuan, Ying, Levine, Liu, Tenenbaum, Choi (2025, COLM) Hypothesis-Driven Theory-of-Mind Reasoning for LLMs (thought-tracing)
finding: An inference-time routine that traces what each agent believes and weights hypotheses by observations (thought-tracing, TT) beats plain and CoT prompting on four ToM benchmarks and beats most reasoning models, with far fewer tokens. Closes part of gap 1: a SimToM-like explicit mental-state filter still helps strong models, and reasoning models do not fix social reasoning.
numbers: ParaphrasedToMi avg: GPT-4o 59.5, +CoT 67.0, +TT 76.0, +TT+CoT 74.3; o1-medium 70.8; o3-mini-medium 64.0; R1 68.3. FANToM All-Qs: GPT-4o 11.1, +TT 41.5, +TT+CoT 54.7; o1-medium 30.2; o3-mini-medium 0.0; R1 37.9. MMToM-QA avg: GPT-4o 56.5, +TT+CoT 69.0, o1-medium 76.0, R1 49.0.
quote: reinforcing mathematical or programming reasoning does not generalize to social reasoning
limits: Authors' own method; text extract of Table 2 partly garbled for some o3-mini cells; GPT-4o-era base models; o1 beats TT on MMToM-QA.
agent_relevance: Supports a built-in 'who knows what' tracing step for social tasks. Do not assume extra reasoning tokens substitute for it.

source: Kim et al. 2025 (same paper), reasoning-model false/true belief trade-off
finding: Reasoning models are near-perfect on false-belief items but collapse on the easier true-belief items (over-reasoning). Vanilla CoT also lowers true-belief scores in closed models.
numbers: ParaphrasedToMi false/true belief: o1-low 98.5/37.0; o1-high 97.0/49.0; R1 77.0/59.5; GPT-4o 38.5/80.5; GPT-4o+CoT 76.0/58.0. Text says o1 and o3-mini true-belief scores fall below 50 and below 30 in some cases. All models 96-99 on BigToM average.
limits: Row alignment of the text extract is imperfect for o3-mini effort levels; the trade-off pattern itself is stated explicitly in the text.
agent_relevance: Test social probes on BOTH false-belief and true-belief variants. A model that always assumes ignorance scores well on false-belief items only.

source: Kim et al. 2025 (same paper), token-use analysis
finding: Wrong answers from reasoning models use more tokens than right ones on ParaphrasedToMi but not on MMToM-QA. GPT-4o with TT scores about 10 points above o1-low and o3-mini-low on ToMi with far fewer output tokens; on MMToM-QA GPT-4o+TT+CoT matches o3-mini-medium at under half the tokens.
numbers: ToMi: GPT-4o+TT 76.0, +TT+CoT 74.3 vs o1-low 67.8; MMToM-QA GPT-4o+TT+CoT 69.0 vs R1 49.0.
limits: Token counts are from figures described in the text; one benchmark family.
agent_relevance: At equal tokens a structured tracing step beats more free reasoning (answers gap 1 partly).

source: Tyen, Mansoor, Carbune, Chen, Mak (2024, ACL Findings) LLMs cannot find reasoning errors, but can correct them given the error location
finding: The bottleneck of self-correction is finding the mistake, not fixing it. With the true mistake location, backtracking helps; with a random location it helps less and costs more on correct traces.
numbers: BIG-Bench Mistake: 300 traces per task, 85% incorrect and 15% correct. GPT-4 overall step-level mistake finding 52.87. Oracle-location backtracking, change in accuracy on originally correct / incorrect traces: tracking shuffled objects -11.11 / +23.53; multistep arithmetic -6.67 / +43.92; Dyck -11.43 / +36.86. Random location: -15.56 / +11.76, -6.67 / +20.39, -13.33 / +21.57.
limits: Oracle labels are not available in practice; only 45 correct traces per task; PaLM 2 wrote the traces; 2023 models. A small trained classifier at about 65% accuracy already gives net gain.
agent_relevance: Where revision hurts is the 'is this wrong?' judgement. Gate revision on an external check or a localised error flag, not a bare 'reconsider' prompt (gap 4).

source: Kamoi, Zhang, Zhang, Han, Zhang (2024, TACL) When Can LLMs Actually Correct Their Own Mistakes? A Critical Survey
finding: No prior work shows successful self-correction from prompted-LLM feedback alone, except on tasks that suit it (decomposable responses, easy feedback). It works with reliable external feedback and after large-scale fine-tuning. Many positive reports use oracle information or weak baselines. Version 3 adds a note on RL-trained o1 and SCoRe as an emerging exception.
quote: no prior work demonstrates successful self-correction with feedback from prompted LLMs
limits: Covers to mid-2024; reasoning-model era only briefly noted.
agent_relevance: Confirms Huang 2023 broadly. For our agent: revise only with an external signal or a trained verifier.

source: Kumar et al. (2024) Training Language Models to Self-Correct via Reinforcement Learning (SCoRe)
finding: Multi-turn RL on the model's own correction traces makes self-correction work where supervised fine-tuning collapses. Intrinsic revision is trainable, not just promptable.
numbers: Abstract: +15.6% self-correction on MATH and +9.1% on HumanEval over base models (Gemini 1.0 Pro and 1.5 Flash).
limits: Abstract page only; Gemini models; needs training, which a scaffold cannot do.

source: Strachan et al. (2024, Nature Human Behaviour) Testing theory of mind in large language models and humans
finding: Closes part of gap 6 for Strachan (full text via Europe PMC). GPT-4 matches or beats humans on false belief, hinting, irony and strange stories but not on faux pas. The faux pas failure is hyperconservatism: GPT-4 will not commit to 'speaker did not know'. Reworded as 'which is more likely' it is perfect.
numbers: 15 independent chats per LLM per test against 250 humans; follow-ups used 1,907 humans in total (900 belief-likelihood, 757 false-belief perturbation). False belief at ceiling for humans and LLMs. Faux pas: only 2 of 349 GPT responses said the speaker knew. Likelihood wording: GPT-4 100% correct unprompted; GPT-3.5 about 3% needed a prompt, about 9% failed. On one other test GPT-4 did not differ from humans (Z=-0.06, P=0.110, r=0.24); LLaMA2-70B was lower (Z=-0.13, P=0.005, r=0.41). Novel items matched original items (all P>0.085).
limits: 2023 model versions; LLaMA2 faux-pas superiority judged illusory (bias to ascribe ignorance).
agent_relevance: Ask for the most likely mental state, not a yes/no on knowledge. This removes over-caution in social probes.

source: Torabi, Nikfarjam, Karami Dorcheh (2026, Annals of General Psychiatry) MCT and depressive symptoms: systematic review, meta-regression, meta-analysis
finding: Newest MCT depression meta-analysis: 51 studies (33 trials). Large effects against waitlist; authors themselves note small samples and a lack of active comparison groups.
numbers: Within-group Hedges g -2.29 (95% CI -2.75 to -1.83). Between-group vs control g -1.28 (95% CI -1.71 to -0.86).
limits: Mostly waitlist comparators; no allegiance analysis in the abstract.
agent_relevance: Does not close the CBT contrast in gap 7. Headline numbers still rest on waitlist data.

source: Gjengedal et al. (2025, eClinicalMedicine) MCT plus work focus for depression or anxiety on sick leave: open-label RCT, Norway
finding: A registry-outcome RCT with blinded assessors: MCT plus work focus about doubles return to work and cuts symptoms versus delayed treatment. Wells is a co-author, so allegiance is not removed.
numbers: N=236 (121 immediate, 115 waitlist), 2017-2020. Return to work at 12 weeks 39% (47/121) vs 20% (23/115), OR 2.39 (95% CI 1.32-4.32). Anxiety time-by-group -8.35; depression -10.84 (both p<0.0001).
limits: Waitlist control; open label; Norwegian welfare context.
agent_relevance: Clinical only. None for the agent.

source: Anwar, Younas, Deebani, Yingjie (2026, Depression and Anxiety) MCT for OCD: three-wave multisite RCT, Pakistan
finding: Independent, assessor-blinded RCT versus treatment as usual: MCT clearly better on clinician-rated OCD severity, but the proposed mechanism (belief change leading symptom change) was NOT supported.
numbers: N=76 (38 MCT, 38 TAU), 12 sessions. Y-BOCS post: MCT 25.2 vs TAU 29.2, diff -4.00, Hedges g -1.12. 6-month: 21.2 vs 28.2, diff -6.92, g -1.54. Lagged indirect effect through beliefs beta=-0.01.
limits: TAU comparator, not CBT or ERP; 6-month follow-up only. Belief domains behaved as state markers, not proximal mechanisms.
agent_relevance: Weakens the clean S-REF story that beliefs about thinking drive change. Another reason not to port MCT mechanisms to the agent.

source: Exner et al. (cited in Anwar 2026) MCT vs ERP non-inferiority RCT in OCD
finding: Head-to-head against first-line ERP. MCT was non-inferior at post-treatment, but non-inferiority was not confirmed at 6-month follow-up. So against an active comparator MCT looks comparable, not clearly better.
numbers: N=74 outpatients, 12 weekly sessions (second-hand, from the citing paper).
limits: Second hand: only the sentence in Anwar 2026 was read; original not opened.
agent_relevance: Supports caution in claims K11 and K12.

source: Petersen, Santoft et al. (2026, Trials) Transdiagnostic MCT vs disorder-specific CBT for anxiety disorders: trial protocol
finding: Protocol, no results yet. It states only one adequately powered trial of transdiagnostic MCT vs disorder-specific CBT exists (d=0.70 favouring MCT post-treatment, inpatient), and that only about 50% of CBT patients remit. An independent Swedish trial is now running.
numbers: Planned N=86 (GAD, social anxiety, PTSD). Prior trial d=0.70 at post-treatment.
agent_relevance: Gap 7 stays open for independent head-to-head data. Wait for this trial.

source: Detached mindfulness as a stand-alone intervention: systematic review and meta-analysis (2026)
finding: Detached mindfulness (noticing intrusive thoughts without engaging them, the core MCT technique) alone: 14 studies, 12 independent samples, N=256. Large pooled effect in only three clinical trials (OCD x2, panic x1). Eight of nine other experimental samples reported a benefit.
numbers: Pooled Hedges g for primary outcomes -1.80 (95% CI -2.84 to -0.76), k=3. Depressive symptoms g -1.15 (95% CI -2.23 to -0.08).
limits: Three clinical samples, wide CIs, humans only. Authors call it converging but limited.
agent_relevance: Gap 5: no LLM test exists. The only analogue is a prompt step that observes a draft thought without acting on it. Untested.

source: Interpersonal alignment of neural evidence accumulation to social exchange of confidence (2023, eLife)
finding: Human work from the confidence-sharing line, with a discovery sample plus pre-registered replication: reported confidence and pupil-inferred uncertainty follow social information. Shows the effect is replicable in humans, but gives no Bahrami 2010 numbers.
numbers: Abstract level only (discovery plus preregistered replication design).
limits: Bahrami 2010 (PMC3371582) returned an empty full-text record from Europe PMC. The exact 2010 numbers remain unverified from open text.
agent_relevance: Gap 6 half closed: Strachan numbers verified, Bahrami 2010 not.

source: Search record: LLM replication of Bahrami confidence-weighted merging or Mahmoodi equality bias (gaps 3 and 6)
finding: Europe PMC queries on 'equality bias' with language models, and on LLM confidence with collective decision-making, found no paper testing Bahrami-style confidence-weighted merging in LLMs. arXiv, Semantic Scholar and OpenAlex APIs returned 429 and the WebSearch budget was spent, so absence is not proven.
numbers: 0 direct LLM replications found. Two tangential hits not opened (ChatGPT confidence judgements 2026; metacognitive sensitivity and AI trust, PNAS Nexus 2025).
limits: Search-limited. Treat as not found, not as nonexistent.
agent_relevance: Gap 3 stays open. Run our own two-run merge test against the stronger run alone at equal tokens.

source: Search record: reasoning models on Hi-ToM order 3+ (gap 9), 2025-2026 intrinsic revision with external-signal control (gap 4), Demetriou ordering (gap 8)
finding: No Hi-ToM order-3+ result for reasoning models was found. The nearest evidence is thought-tracing on first-order tasks, where o1, o3-mini and R1 are inconsistent. No 2025-2026 paper with reasoning models plus an external-signal control for revision was located. No source linking Demetriou's developmental order to LLM capability order was found.
limits: Rate-limited APIs and spent WebSearch budget. Not exhaustive.
